result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.has_cycles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph contains any cycles. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9344-L9382){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.has_cycles() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses depth-first search to detect cycles. For directed graphs, looks for back edges. For undirected graphs, checks for cycles excluding trivial two-node back-and-forth paths. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph contains at least one cycle, `False` if acyclic. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#04c9d200 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) graph.has_cycles() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Adding an edge back from "C" to "A" closes the loop, so the graph now contains a cycle: ::: {#aabdfbe2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_edge("C", "A") graph.has_cycles() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
